input.question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?
input.ground_truth: Certainly if one considers the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid empire as the "end of antiquity" and the beginning of the early medieval era. It is the last great war because the next one defined the end of the era. Then the question becomes is the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire the best delimiting event between late antiquity and early medieval. There's a lot of good points stating that it is, since the fall of the Sassanid empire meant the Byzantine Empire was then the only surviving great power from classical antiquity. All of the other powers of the era are relatively new. The Muslim conquest of North Africa and Levant also split off those regions from what the classical Roman world. A parallel can be drawn to how the fall of the Soviet Union marked the end of the cold war.

Question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of old toys. These toys are from a time we call “antiquity”—that’s a fancy word for a long time ago, when people like the Greeks and Romans played.

Now, there was a really big fight (we call it a “war”) between two leaders: Heraclius and Khusro II. This fight happened a long, long time ago, around 1,600 years ago.

James Howard-Johnston, who is like a grown-up who studies these old stories, called this war “the last great war of antiquity.” That means he thinks it was the final super big and important fight before the world changed into something new.

But was he right? Well, think about this: after this war, lots of things changed. The big Roman Empire in the east (which we call Byzantium) became even more different from the old Roman Empire. New ideas and new kinds of people started to take over. The world started to look less like the old world of the Greeks and Romans and more like the world we know today.

So, James Howard-Johnston thought this war was the last “big kid” fight from the old times, before everything started changing a lot. He thought after this, the old ways were finished, and new ways began.

So, in a simple way:  
James Howard-Johnston called this war “the last great war of antiquity” because after it, the old world of the Greeks and Romans was almost gone, and a new world was starting. He thought it was the final big, important fight from that old time.
